records.name: Minnesota
records.summary: This state went furthest on non-cooperation: a 2023 law declares anti-trans law enacted elsewhere against this state's public policy and bars cooperation with warrants, arrests and extradition related to gender-affirming care, a state refusing to help enforce hostility enacted elsewhere. A July 2026 national risk map lists this state in its most-protective tier, among the safest legal environments for a trans visitor in the country and clearly above the national average.

sources.summary: Minnesota Session Law 2023 ch. 29 (HF 146): gender-affirming health care as defined in the Act 'is against the public policy of this state and must not be enforced or applied' in pending cases; the law amends provisions on warrants, arrests and extraditions related to out-of-state laws on gender-affirming health care.
July 2026 assessment lists Minnesota among 'Most Protective States (CA, CO, CT, HI, IL, MA, MD, MN, NJ...)', the tier the piece treats as strongest.

records.name: Rhode Island
records.summary:
“Most Protective” tier in the July 2026 assessment: regional non-discrimination covering gender identity and shield/refuge protections enforceable against out-of-state actions.

No state-specific negative finding beyond the shared federal layer (passport/API policy).

sources.summary: July 2026 anti-trans legal risk assessment map: Rhode Island listed among the 'Most Protective' states (gender-identity nondiscrimination tier); the page also reports federal-layer erosion (DC House bathroom ban) meaning the top tier 'can no longer be considered most protective' nationwide.

mapresearch.org transgender healthcare equality map: nationwide tracker of states with shield laws or executive orders (2023 and 2024 batches) making protections enforceable against out-of-state action; Rhode Island appears among the shield-law/executive-order jurisdictions and the full all-jurisdictions directory.
